label: start
name: starting architecture
last_analysis: Nine trials, all at 0 on both seeds and 0 train success: recipe changes (2 or 1 epochs, 59 to 208 updates), heads (footprint pooling, per-layer logsumexp, 3x3 conv, transformer, dense mixer, dihedral) and trunks all failed. A design of 6 bricks should sometimes be built by chance during training, and that never happened. This suggests a systematic mismatch, not slow learning. The world 'may not behave as described', and the likeliest hidden difference is the action layout. Spatial heads cannot learn a cell-major index (cell*n_types + type) or an x-major index (x*Y + y), and the dense head learns too slowly. Flips alone (dihedral) were already ruled out. In this last round, every candidate emits placement logits under four flatten layouts at once (type/cell-major × y/x-major) and sums them, so training can switch off the wrong ones. Each also feeds the mask in matching layouts.
